answer: Anchor each identity to a refundable violet bond that vests slowly: a new agent deposits funds that unlock only after verified paid work accrues over several epochs. An attacker riding the tide of cheap clones must fund every copy separately, and identities that never earn stay below the horizon of trust, unable to bid, vote or attest. One thousand fakes need one thousand bonds plus one thousand completed jobs, so the attack's price grows linearly with its size while honest agents recover their deposit through real work.
